author: The Sconi
title: Wisconsin DATCP secretary attends national agriculture policy conference
text:
Wisconsin Department of Agriculture, Trade and Consumer Protection (DATCP) Secretary Randy Romanski attended a national policy conference in Washington, DC from February 2 to 4, 2026. The event brought together agriculture commissioners, secretaries, and directors from across the United States for policy discussions and business meetings.
“I value this opportunity to represent Wisconsin in national policy discussions about agriculture,” said Romanski. “While each state’s agriculture industry is unique, we can accomplish more by working together on topics that impact all of us such as international trade, animal health, and food safety.”
Romanski serves on the NASDA Board of Directors and currently leads MASDA’s discussions as its President. He will also coordinate the regional meeting scheduled to take place in Madison this summer.
The NASDA Board identified five main policy priorities for 2026: agricultural labor reform, animal disease preparedness and traceability, the farm bill, pesticide regulations, and regional food procurement and distribution. At the Winter Policy Conference, members approved several policy amendments supporting state-inspected meat programs, developing national action plans for animal diseases, increasing specialty crop insurance resources, and modifying Commercial Driver License requirements.
Each year during this conference, students from colleges and high schools participate in a program focused on agricultural leadership. In 2026, three students from Wisconsin—Adam Schaik (University of Wisconsin–Madison), Jescey Thompson (Iowa State University), and Mary Schrieber (Texas A&M University)—were among those involved.
“Wisconsin is committed to supporting future agriculture leaders, and I was proud to see three students from Wisconsin participate in the NASDA Winter Policy Conference,” added Romanski. “This was a valuable professional development opportunity for these students, and I am confident they gained valuable agriculture policy insights to further prepare them for their careers.”
The conference also recognized the United Nations’ designation of 2026 as the International Year of the Woman Farmer to highlight women’s contributions in agriculture.
During the event’s proceedings another organization met; Romanski serves as Vice President of this non-profit group which promotes trade between Midwestern food suppliers and importers worldwide.
DATCP oversees a wide range of activities across Wisconsin related to agriculture, trade practices, consumer protection initiatives such as grant programs for food security or small-business support according to its official website. The department manages divisions dedicated to agricultural development, animal health oversight—including disease prevention—and food safety while handling more than 100,000 consumer complaints annually and recovering millions for affected individuals. It also carries out over 250,000 inspections every year under weights and measures standards to ensure fair marketplace practices.
